content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents an ensemble method for object detection, which improves the detection performance and resistance to four existing evasion attacks. The proposed method is named ODEN. It consists of two parts: (1) inconsistency solver that aggregates predictions from a group of object detectors; (2) diversity-based ensemble selection to select models from a pool of object detectors. Experiments are carried out on three popular detection datasets. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths

-[motivation] recent attacks pose security concerns to object detectors, but the defense side is still under-explored. The motivation and insights in section 1 are clear.

-[effectiveness] in non-adversarial case, the ensemble method achieves better performance than the best individual model. In adversarial case, the method provides the best performance over existing methods.

Weaknesses

-[quality/reference] a concise but comprehensive view on attacks and defense for object detection is provided in section 2. However, object detection, attack, and defense in the classification domain should be briefly reviewed as well. For instance, an ensemble of weak defenses is found not strong enough (Adversarial Example Defenses: Ensembles of Weak Defenses are not Strong, WOOT 2017 by Nicolas Carlini). Meanwhile, Adaptive attacks against proposed defenses may exist (Obfuscated Gradients Give a False Sense of Security: Circumventing Defenses to Adversarial Examples, ICML18, and On Adaptive Attacks to Adversarial Example Defenses, NIPS2020 by Madry). These works are relevant and important to this topic, even if this paper focuses on object detection solely.

-[adaptive attack and assumption, major] More about the adaptive attack and broken assumption. The proposed ensemble method deeply relies on the assumption that the models independently produce different failure modes against an attack. Once the assumption is broken (e.g., an adaptive attack that results in a consistent failure mode among the models), the proposed method will provide a false sense of security. In paragraph 2 of section 1, we can see that the ensemble size is small, so it is more convenient for an adaptive attacker to target all models in the ensemble. Here is another detailed possibility of adaptive attack. One solution in phase III of section 3.1 is "if the group contains ... from only a few member models, ... less likely to corresponding to a real entity ...". An adaptive attack can be designed designed to make most models unable to detect an object? (alghtough this is not used by default).

-[ablation, minor] in section 3.1, it is described that "the learn to calibrate is used by default". How does it compare to other alternatives presented in this paper?

-[complexity, minor] The proposed ensemble method is effective, but is complicated. This is reflected by the fact the algorithm procedure takes three pages of pure text. This makes it uneasy to follow the idea of the proposed method. Most importantly, I think it will be very difficult to reproduce the complicated process with the text once the code is unavailable.

-[suggestion] Since the design is already complicated enough, I'd suggest the author remove unnecessary alternative designs (like the non-default solutions in section 3.1) to confuse readers. Anyway, these alternative designs are not reflected in tables.

-[clarity, minor] at the beginning of section 3, the ||.|| (difference between two sets of object detection results) is undefined anywhere in the manuscript. Meanwhile, this "difference metric" is not used in the whole section 3. Does that mean Eq.(1) is not actually implemented in code form, but just conveys an idea of what the ensemble method is trying to achieve?

-[experiment, minor] standard deviation should be reported when measuring time consumption in section 4.3.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
-[clarity] it is hard to follow a three-page algorithm described by text.

-[quality] some important references (incl. adaptive attack) are not cited.

-[novelty] ODEN is a manually designed object detector ensemble method.

-[reproducibility] python code is available. But I worry that it would be very difficult to implement the method following the text.
content.summary_of_the_review: The proposed method is a manually designed ensemble method for detectors. It achieves good performance in non-adversarial setting. However, its complexity makes the paper not easy to follow. Adaptive attack and broken assumptions (limitations of the method) are not mentioned at all (which may bring us a false sense of security). Based on these and some other clarity issues, I'd preliminarily recommend a weak reject.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The authors address the problem of building ensembles of object detection models that are resilient to adversarial attacks. To do so, they proceed in two steps:

1. A "merging" procedure that combines the outputs of $n$ models (predicted class, confidence score, and boundaries)
2. An algorithm that, given $n$ candidate members, chooses the sub-ensemble of size $k$ of highest focal diversity.

They verify across several types of adversarial attacks on neural nets that these combined steps, dubbed ODEN,  improve the mAP evaluation metric for object detection tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
# Strengths
- The authors address an interesting problem through the lens of ensembling -- a simple, powerful technique that achieves SOTA for a variety of classification and regression tasks. Extending this analysis to object detection is a natural, valuable contribution.
- Empirical results conclusively show that ODEN significantly increases reliability against adversarial attacks.
- Authors provide an ablation study, showing that the first step in aggregating predictions is responsible for the very large majority of the improved performance under adversarial attacks.

# Weaknesses
- If I understand correct the grouping process, the predictions of individual models for non-predicted classes are discarded (ie, if model A predicts a dog with probability 0.5 and a cat with probability 0.49, the latter is discarded). Is my understanding correct? If so, would it be possible / valuable to extend ODEN to include secondary classes?
- Lack of complexity analysis: Given the exponential time cost of enumerating sub-ensembles of a larger set (as described $\S 3.2$), please provide the time complexity for the overall ensemble selection.
- It isn't clear whether the other considered baselines are also ensemble-based (or at least, leverage the same order-of-magnitude compute during training and make similar assumptions about compute and memory allocation).
- Authors should be careful to provide some justification, and, when relevant, a few sentences describing terms from previous literature that are immediately relevant to their work, such as "focal diversity". In this case, I would recommend the authors describing the key contributions of (Wu, 2021b) in the main text.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
**Quality**: Due to the clarity issues discussed below, and in particular due to the fact that it is not clear whether the compared approaches in the experimental section are all ensemble-based, I look forward to the discussion period to evaluate this more clearly.

**Clarity**: I found this paper somewhat difficult to read. The authors should consider shortening the long, verbose paragraphs describing the components of their algorithm (especially in page 6) by including the shortened pseudocode in the main text. As it is, understanding the ensemble selection is particularly difficult. In addition, I strongly recommend the authors spend more time discussing in more depth several relevant works, rather than simply citing them. In particular: (Wu, 2021b), as well as the baselines considered in the experimental section: how do they compare to ODEN in terms of parameter count and time complexity (not only serving time inference)?

**Originality**: I am not an expert in the detailed CV literature; however, ensembling, which accounts for the majority of the improvements by ODEN, is -- although not a novel idea -- an important tool to understand in detail, as are the different methods for aggregating predictions that are not amenable for simple mean-aggregation. Can the authors comment on a comparison to _Ensemble Methods for Object Detection_ (Casado-Garcia & Heras, 2020)?
content.summary_of_the_review:
This is an interesting paper; applying ensembles to object detection is a natural task given the performance of ensembles on classification and regression tasks.

However, there are significant enough clarity issues in this paper that I do not believe it is currently ready for acceptance to ICLR.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces ODEN, a novel approach to object detection ensemble, which combines a detection inconsistency solver with focal diversity-optimized ensemble pruning to defend against evasion attacks. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks show that ODEN can outperform existing ensemble methods in benign while under four evasion attacks, ODEN can maintain high mAP.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
- Introduce ODEN, a novel approach to object detection ensemble
- Comprehensive evaluation of benign and adversarial demonstrating its high effectiveness. 

Weakness:
- Table format issue

In this paper, there are some tables that exceed the boundary of the text. For instance, Table 4 exceeds the boundary a lot. Also, Table 5 and 6 also exceed the boundary. Not sure whether ICLR has such format constraints. I recommend the authors could improve the format of this paper.

- No adaptive attack 

There is no adaptive attack discussed in the paper. ODEN leverage the inconsistency of the detection results. Such designs by nature are vulnerable to simultaneous attacks, i.e., attack all the detection models at the same time, which thus cannot make these methods fundamentally defend against adversarial attacks. Also, some papers show that the evasion attacks can be transferred to different models such as "Fooling the Eyes of Autonomous Vehicles: Robust Physical Adversarial Examples Against Traffic Sign Recognition Systems" published in NDSS 2022. This supports that it is highly possible to launch an adaptive attack to attack the defense based on inconsistency. Thus, the authors should discuss more on the adaptive attack part, especially simultaneous attacks.

- Lack of justification for the attack selections

In this paper, four attacks are selected: TOG, EUA, RAP, and DAG. But there is no support or justifications for why these four attacks are selected. Are these four more representative or powerful than others? The authors should define their own criteria for the attack selection. For instance, there is a new one "ADC: Adversarial attacks against object Detection that evade Context consistency checks" published in WACV 2022. In general, if they only evaluate the attacks which are less powerful or representative, it will be unclear whether their designs are useful or not.

- Lack of practicality evaluation

This paper is motivated by some real-world systems such as autonomous vehicles and intelligent surveillance. However, in the evaluation part, there are no such evaluations. It is unclear whether their designs can be applied to a real-world system or not and whether their computation cost can be tolerated by real-time systems such as autonomous driving systems. Thus, I would recommend the authors to perform more evaluation to demonstrate the practicality of their designs

- Lack of comparison with existing defense

There exist lots of defenses for object detection such as using adversarial training "Towards Adversarially Robust Object Detection" published in ICCV 2019. However, there is no comparison with these potential baselines. If the existing work can already outperform their proposed method, their designs will be less useful. Thus, it would be better if the authors could compare with the baselines.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is easy to read and follow and it looks novel. But I have some major concern about its format, adaptive attack, justification about the attack selections, practicality, and comparison with potential baseline.
content.summary_of_the_review:
This paper introduce a novel design ODEN which can defend against the evasion attack.

However, the paper has following limitations:

- Table format issue

- No adaptive attack 

- Lack of justification for the attack selections

- Lack of practicality evaluation

- Lack of comparison with existing defense
